Under 'Über das Projekt' it says 'Google errichtet derzeit ein hochmodernes Rechenzentrum in Kronstorf, Oberösterreich' (Google is currently building a state-of-the-art data centre in Kronstorf, Upper Austria), that commissioning is planned for 2027 with 100 direct jobs, and that 'Im Rahmen des Baus des Rechenzentrums beschäftigt Google derzeit über 200 österreichische Unternehmen' (for the construction of the data centre Google currently employs more than 200 Austrian companies), naming several construction, crane, gravel/concrete and electrical contractors. It says the energy demand will rise step by step once Google ramps up operation in the initial phase at 150 MW, possibly to up to 500 MW if Google decides to expand, and that cooling uses bank filtrate of the Enns with a water-law maximum of 15,200 m3 per day at full build-out. This is a dated present-tense operator statement that the data centre is under construction. The 2027 commissioning is a forecast, and 150/500 MW describe power demand stages, not built or operating IT capacity.

The plan area is parcels 5k Gellerup, Varde Jorder, part of 207, 135d, 135e, 143e, 143i, 143k and 143n Varde Markjorder and parts of Roustvej, added to the parcels of the 2023 idea phase; most of the area south of Roustvej is covered by lokalplan 23.03.L08 (adopted August 2021, business area for data centres), shown inside the red application boundary in Figure 3. Access is from Roustvej via Ostre Omfartsvej. No permit, operator, tenant or construction date is stated.

johor-batam-p10-dayone-ktp-wtp-release-2.summary: DayOne's release of 5 November 2026 says DayOne 'today announced' the Phase 2 expansion of its Kempas Tech Park Water Treatment Plant (KTP-WTP) in Johor, which will double the plant's self-treated water capacity to 20 million litres a day. It says the expansion builds on Phase 1 of DayOne's operating KTP-WTP, which has been operational since March 2026 and 'has already been providing capacity above current requirements, eliminating the campus' reliance on municipal potable water for data center cooling'; Phase 2 is expected to begin operations in the third quarter of 2027. johor-batam-p10-ytlp-annual-report-2026.summary: YTL Power International's 336-page Annual Report 2026 covers the financial year ended 30 June 2026. Its Data Center segmental review (PDF page 32) says that the Data Center segment comprises YTL Data Center's development, construction, ownership and operation of data centres in Malaysia; that the flagship YTL Green Data Center Park in Kulai, Johor, has had its planned capacity increased to up to 1,200 MW from 600 MW; that 'a total of 298 MW is currently contracted, with progress on new phases well underway'; that the data centres are principally let to third parties under medium- to long-term leases; and that the first 215 MWac phase of the co-located solar facility has been implemented. The review of results (page 22) says Data Center segment revenue rose to RM867.1 million from RM124.1 million, 'driven by the progressive ramp-up of data halls', and that profit rose on the progressive completion and occupancy ramp-up of additional data halls. The Executive Chairman's statement (page 9) says new capacity is coming onstream at the Kulai campus; the AI cloud review (page 33) says the first phase of YTL AI Cloud is based at the park; and the List of Properties as at 30 June 2026 (page 155) lists Kulai Young Estate, Kulai, Johor (freehold, 6,639,761 m2) as data centres, a consumer landing station and land held for the solar facility and future data-centre phases, with 205,451 m2 built up and buildings aged 6 months to 2.7 years. The report also describes the separate proposed YTL/JLand gigawatt-scale campus at Sedenak Tech Park West announced in August 2026 (about 145 acres, option on 400 more). 1,200 MW is planned capacity and 298 MW is contracted capacity; neither is built or measured load.
johor-batam-p10-ytlp-annual-report-2026.title: YTL Power International Berhad Annual Report 2026 (financial year ended 30 June 2026; dated 30 October 2026)

mexico-ca-p9-qro-cloudhq-reunion-2026100.summary: Querétaro state executive press release. It reports that the governor received a delegation from CloudHQ at the Palacio de la Corregidora to discuss progress on the company's investment project in the state, developed together with the state government, to install a campus of six data centres. It says the meeting was the occasion to announce an increase in the project's energy capacity, entirely at the US company's cost, from 250 MW to almost 1,000 MW, and that CloudHQ said total project financing will rise from US$4.8 billion to almost US$6 billion. It closes by saying the executives presented to the authorities an update on the works and the details of the project's execution schedule, whose progress was said to remain on the established timetable. The release does not say that data-centre buildings are under construction, complete or operating, and gives no site address.

us-west-p10-em-cc-packet-20261020.summary: The agenda (item 14.A background) states that 'Corrigan Farms LLC seeks to rezone parcel number 59:068:0006 to add the RTI overlay zone to the property to allow it to potentially develop a data center project with a natural gas power plant.' The development-agreement staff report (item 14.B) says the agreement 'accompanies the rezone of a 41-acre parcel owned by Corrigan Farms LLC to the RTI Overlay Zone and establishes development and infrastructure requirements for the anticipated data center project', that the parcel 'abuts other data center properties', that the agreement is consistent with other data center development agreements except for a 20-year term, and that 'It is anticipated that the applicant will construct 2 data centers with an on site natural gas power plant.' The attached draft agreement (Draft 10-13) between the City and Corrigan Farms, LLC recites that the Company owns approximately 40.99 acres of undeveloped land and proposes a multi-phase Project with 'the uses of one or more data centers' and related power, cooling and electrical facilities; it vests no power-generation rights and lists the remaining approvals (RTI site plan by the Development Review Committee, plats, grading permit, building permits). The rezone staff report gives 40.99 acres, adjacent to existing RTI on the north, east and south, notes that QTS currently uses the property for temporary operational trailers, and its exhibit map marks the subject property south of 1000 North Street beside the QTS and Meta campuses; the presentation says there is no development proposal at this time.

locator.precision: Area-weighted centre of the official BEV cadastral envelopes (axis-aligned bounding rectangles served by the BEV Katasterviewer API) of all 15 parcels named in the Bezirkshauptmannschaft Linz-Land permit of 16 December 2025: Gst 1454/1, 1454/5, 1455, 1456, 1457, 1458/1, 1458/2, 1459, 1460/2, 1461/1, 1462/1 and 1463/1, KG Stallbach (45113), and Gst 1243/2, 1277/1 and 1278, KG Kronstorf (45106). Each envelope centre is weighted by its BEV register area (49.19 ha in all); the computation is in EPSG:31255 (MGI / Austria GK Central). The point lies inside the envelopes of Gst 1456 (15.0 ha) and 1458/1 (4.7 ha), the two southern parcels; the union of the envelopes spans about 817 m east-west by 1,166 m north-south. locator.uncertainty_reason: The BEV API publishes parcel envelopes, not outlines, so the point approximates the centre of the permitted site and is not proven to lie inside a parcel outline (it is inside two parcel envelopes).
